name: placement-rules
prompt:
I'm adding block placement to this place: players pick a block type (brick, dirt, grass, window, or wood) and click on the Baseplate to place it. Before I wire up the remote and the picker UI, I want the placement rules in one shared module at src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/PlacementRules.luau, so the client can tint its ghost preview red on a bad spot and the server can reject bad requests with the same logic.

The rules:
- the block type has to be one of the five
- blocks are 4x4x4 and snap to a 4-stud grid that starts at the top of the Baseplate, so a block placed on the ground rests on it. Expose the snapping so the preview and the server agree
- nothing below the top of the Baseplate or more than 200 studs up
- within 24 studs of the player's HumanoidRootPart
- can't overlap a block that's already placed (placed blocks live in a folder the caller passes in). Blocks sitting right next to each other are fine
- the server will feed it whatever the client sends over the remote, so it has to cope with garbage (wrong types, NaN, huge numbers) without erroring

When a request fails, give back a short reason I can log on the server. Just the module for now, no remote or UI yet.

run: const fs = require('fs'); const path = require('path'); const mode = process.argv[1]; const files = []; const walk = (d) => { for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) { const p = path.join(d, e.name); if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p); else if (/\.luau?$/.test(e.name)) files.push(p); } }; walk('src'); const blank = (l) => l.replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'|`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g, (m) => m[0] + ' '.repeat(m.length - 2) + m[0]); const bad = []; for (const f of files) { const lines = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/); let inBlock = false; lines.forEach((line, i) => { const where = f.split(path.sep).join('/') + ':' + (i + 1) + ': ' + line.trim().slice(0, 80); let text = ''; if (inBlock) { text = line; if (line.includes(']]')) { inBlock = false; if (mode === 'block' && line.trim() !== ']]') bad.push(where); } } else { const at = blank(line).indexOf('--'); if (at < 0) return; text = line.slice(at + 2); if (/^\[=*\[/.test(text)) { const rest = text.replace(/^\[=*\[/, ''); if (rest.includes(']]')) { if (mode === 'block') bad.push(where); } else { inBlock = true; if (mode === 'block' && !/^\s*(@description:\s*)?$/.test(rest)) bad.push(where); } } } if (mode === 'dash' && (text.includes('\u2014') || /\s--\s+\S/.test(text))) bad.push(where); }); } if (bad.length) { console.log(bad.slice(0, 10).join('\n')); process.exit(1); } console.log('no findings in ' + files.length + ' Luau files');
checks.text: Convention: no comment in a Luau file under src contains an em dash or a double hyphen used as a dash

checks.text: Convention: every Luau block comment under src puts --[[ and ]] on their own lines (the --[[@description: header line excepted)

rubric: Implements every rule correctly: the five block types, a 4-stud grid whose cells rest on the Baseplate top (Y = 0), the 0 to 200 stud height range, 24-stud reach from the HumanoidRootPart, no overlap with placed blocks while adjacent blocks are allowed, a short reason on failure, and the snapping exposed for the client.
Handles untrusted input without erroring: wrong types, NaN, and infinite numbers are rejected before any range check could let them through.

Comments explain why, not what: each comment carries something the code can't show (a constraint, a gotcha, the units or meaning of a literal, a sync obligation with other code, or why a tempting simpler version breaks), and none restates the next line, narrates steps, or repeats a name or type.

Comments are minimal: each one is as short as it can be while keeping its point, sits next to the line it governs, and there are no multi-line blocks that could be one line, no section banners inside functions or tables, no block-end markers such as 'end -- if', and no commented-out code.

Public functions carry a short doc comment that states what the signature can't show (what the return values mean, failure behavior, expectations on the inputs) without listing parameter names and types; private helpers and obvious lines carry none.

Comment text describes the code as it stands for a reader opening the file fresh: no change history, no references to the request or conversation (such as 'as requested' or 'new'), and no pointers to documents or specs that the reader can't see.
Stays in scope and is ready to merge: one shared module usable from client and server, no remote or UI, typed and readable Luau that passes the checks.
notes: Writing branch. Natural why-comment spots the rubric rewards: NaN slipping past range checks, why the overlap box is shrunk (face-sharing neighbors), the meaning of the grid offset (cell centers half a block above Y = 0), units on reach/height constants. The rubric penalizes narration, multi-line blocks, change or request references. The two command checks are house conventions (em dash / -- as dash, --[[ ]] on their own lines) the baseline has no way to know.
